content:
I have been doing many experiments with Aristotle, many of which generate Lean code with a copyright of 2024 (?) and an Apache 2.0 License. These examples I use to learn both about Lean and about Aristotle's capabilities, and as such I have no issue with the headers.

I would like to tweak some files for my own private use. As long as I don't distribute them or harm anyone else with them, that should also be fine, regardless of what license appears in the files.

I am planning to make a public repository which includes blueprints (which I have created without direct assistance by any AI agent) and Aristotle code resulting from the blueprints. I also plan to tweak the Lean code from Aristotle to give annotations from myself, and perhaps alter the code slightly based on suggestions from other sources, perhaps AI-based, perhaps not. The intent will be to preserve the function of the code and comments made by Aristotle and add clarifying remarks and perhaps slightly change the style of presentation in the Lean file(s).

I would not release the blueprints under the Apache license. I would also like to take the amended code and release it under something other than the Apache license, with the intent that people who may use the repository essentially acknowledge the source, but otherwise put no restrictions or warranties on it.

If I am clear about the source that inspired the amended code, can I make such a repository (with a license term that is not Apache 2.0) without creating any problems or hassle for myself and for the entity which provides Aristotle (presumably Harmonic and its representatives)? Besides crediting the source, what else would Harmonic need from me in order that I could make this kind of change?
sender_full_name: J. J. Issai (project started by GRP)
